In [[mathematics]], a '''modular Lie algebra''' is a [[Lie algebra]] over a [[field (mathematics)|field]] of positive [[characteristic (algebra)|characteristic]].

The theory of modular Lie algebras is significantly different from the theory of [[real number|real]] and [[complex number|complex]] Lie algebras. This difference can be traced to the properties of [[Frobenius automorphism]] and to the failure of the [[Lie group#The exponential map|exponential map]] to establish a tight connection between properties of a modular Lie algebra and the corresponding [[algebraic group]].

Although serious study of modular Lie algebras was initiated by [[Nathan Jacobson]] in 1950s, their [[representation theory]] in the [[semisimple Lie algebra|semisimple]] case was advanced only recently due to the influential [[Lusztig conjectures]], which have been partially [[mathematical proof|proved]].
